author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
On the **amount** — $2,000 is correct for this joint filer, because New Mexico enacted **two** unlimited rebates against 2021 returns, not one:
- **§7-2-7.5 "Supplemental 2021 income tax rebates"** (Laws 2022, 3rd S.S., Ch. 2 = the HB 2 you cite): $1,000 joint, paid in two 2022 installments;
- **§7-2-7.7 "Additional 2021 income tax rebates"** (Laws **2023**, Ch. 211 §11): another $1,000 joint, paid June 2023, also keyed to the 2021 PIT return.

The $500 income-limited rebate (HB 163, AGI < $150k joint) is correctly **denied** at this record's ~$237k AGI. So the $1,000 figure counts only HB 2 and misses the 2023 act.

On the **timing** — This is the rebate-timing convention we closed out in #1068: PolicyEngine books one-time rebates to the year whose return determines them; `taxsimtest` default mode books the payment year; and — key point — **your own `opt(27)=1`/`opt(30)=1` (set on this very record's txpydata) books the eligible year, same as PE**. TaxAct returns show neither, since these are administrative payments, not return line items. For comparisons we ship three tools: the `srebate` output column, `compare --net-of-rebates`, and `compare --taxsim-opt30` (#1070/#1074). If you'd rather both engines exclude rebates from `siitax` entirely (matching the TA return), that's `opt(27)=2` on your side and `--net-of-rebates` on ours — happy to converge on that as the standard if you prefer it.
